newsitem.title: USA: Ascend to ship high-speed modem device.
newsitem.headline: Ascend to ship high-speed modem device.

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc said Tuesday it will ship a device to online companies and Internet service providers that can accept calls from a new generation of high-speed modems.
Ascend, a maker of computer networking equipment, will use technology developed by Rockwell International Corp's semiconductor division.
The companies said Ascend's Max switch, to be shipped in January, will let online companies accept calls from customers who are using high-speed.

Modem makers such as US Robotics Corp and Rockwell have announced plans in recent weeks to ship 56,000-baud modems. These devices send or receive about three pages of typed text a second, about twice as fast as the fastest modems currently sold.

The new generation of modems will force online companies, such as America Online Inc. and Netcom On-Line Communication Services Inc., to buy networking equipment that can handle the calls, analysts said.
Ascend, based in Alameda, Calif., is the biggest independent maker of equipment for online services.
In midafternoon trading, Ascend shares were up 3 7/8 at 71 5/8.
-- Kourosh Karimkhany, in Los Angeles, + 1 800 330 NEWS
